key_insight: Four-tetrahedron macro-element condensation shrinks equilibrium-based plasticity Newton systems by an estimated 4× in dimension and structural nonzeros relative to stress-only elimination.
engineering_relevance: Smaller linear systems reduce memory demand and accelerate large-scale 3D elastoplasticity and limit-analysis simulations while retaining statically admissible stress fields.
method: Eliminate stress directions and macro-internal traction-continuity multipliers to obtain reduced systems supporting positive-definite factorization.
Establish global and local nonsingularity conditions, including trace-bound augmentation for von Mises limit analysis.
Use CUDA Fortran batched routines and cuDSS, with an optional preconditioned conjugate-gradient solver for elastoplasticity.
evidence_signal: Reported tests show up to 2× CPU speedup and 66.5% lower peak linear-solver memory versus stress-only elimination, plus GPU speedups up to 13.5× over the CPU counterpart and 87.5× over MOSEK.
watch_item: The lower-memory iterative GPU option increases solution time, and the reported peak speedups should not be assumed across all problem sizes.
paper_title: A GPU Interior-Point Solver with Macro-Element Condensation for Equilibrium-Based Plasticity
